content: I need to add circuit breaker logic to our payment gateway client. Right now if the downstream provider goes down we just hammer it with retries until the timeout cascade takes out the whole service mesh.

A circuit breaker pattern would help here. You'd track failure rates over a sliding window and trip the breaker when failures exceed a threshold, returning a fast error instead of waiting for timeouts. Would you like me to outline the state machine (closed → open → half-open)?

Yeah — the thing is, we already have a half-baked retry wrapper but it doesn't track state across requests. I want something that integrates with our Prometheus metrics so we get observability on trip events. Fundamentally the circuit breaker needs to be per-endpoint, not per-service, because the provider has separate endpoints for auth and capture that fail independently.

That's a good distinction. Per-endpoint breakers give you much finer control. For the Prometheus integration, you'd want counters for trips, resets, and half-open probe results. Here's a Go pattern using a struct per endpoint...

Right, and I want the thresholds configurable via our feature flags system — not hardcoded. The auth endpoint can tolerate maybe 30% failure rate before tripping because it's called way more often, but the capture endpoint should trip at 10% because every failure there is a lost transaction.

Makes sense. You could define a CircuitBreakerConfig struct with fields for failure threshold, window duration, and half-open max probes, then load those from your feature flag system at startup and on change events.

Exactly. And the half-open state needs backpressure — I don't want to flood the recovering endpoint with probe requests. One probe per interval, and if it succeeds we ramp back up gradually. Think exponential ramp-up, not instant close.
So a graduated close: half-open allows 1 request, then 2, 4, 8 up to full traffic. Each successful batch doubles the allowed concurrency. A single failure at any ramp stage re-trips to open.
That's the pattern. I'll prototype it tomorrow — going to use our existing middleware chain so it composes cleanly with the trace propagation and idempotency layers we already have.
